observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: 0x004c49e6 MOV dword ptr [EBP-0xc],ECX spills ECX, which is the __thiscall receiver slot, and 0x004c49a6-region loads read it back. EDX is never read, so the body is not __fastcall. 0x004c4a20 RET 0x4 pops one stack word, which rules out cdecl. Ghidra's own decompilation labels it __thiscall.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: Either the dword stored at receiver+0x18, the dword stored at receiver+0x1c, or the literal 0, chosen by the index argument. Every observed consumer branches on the result being null and then dereferences it, so the value is an object pointer.
observed_original_abi.return_observation: 0x004c4a00 MOV EDX,dword ptr [ECX+0x18] and 0x004c4a10 MOV ECX,dword ptr [EAX+0x1c] are dword loads, and 0x004c4a06 / 0x004c4a16 copy the full 32 bits into EAX. 0x004c4a1b XOR EAX,EAX zeroes all 32 bits, so the default is a dword 0 and not a byte 0.

semantic_contract: Given a non-null receiver R and a 32-bit index i, the function returns R->dword[0x18] when i == 0, R->dword[0x1c] when i == 1, and the literal dword 0 for every other i, including i >= 2 and i == 0xffffffff. The return is a full 32-bit EAX, so a stored null slot is indistinguishable from an out-of-range index: both produce 0, and every observed consumer branches on exactly that, treating a zero as 'absent'. The body reads exactly one dword and mutates nothing, so the function is pure, idempotent and re-entrant. A null receiver is not checked and faults on the selected load. Both arms are live: 0x005ab701 and 0x005ab712 pass index 0 while seventeen inspected sites pass index 1. The default arm is defensive rather than proven-dead, because no observed caller passes an index outside {0,1} but nothing rules one out. Consumers dereference the result at +0x34 (0x005ab717) and at +0x8 (0x0058c585), so the returned value is an object pointer whose type is not established.
classification_rationale: The complete body, the ABI, both field offsets, the comparison order, the branch polarity, the return width and the ret form were read directly from the live binary, and nineteen distinct call sites corroborate the return contract, including two that exercise the index==0 arm. The material element that stays bounded is the identity of the owning type: the receiver provenance is not uniform (cEditor+0x150, cEditor+0x140, and +0xe0 of an unrelated caller object), openspore_vtable_lookup found no vtable slot for this address, and SporeApp.exe has no MSVC RTTI, so no class can be named. What the two slots point at is likewise unresolved: the body never dereferences them and the only observations are the consumers' own +0x8 and +0x34 dereferences. STRONG_SEMANTIC is therefore withheld: the behaviour of the body is fully determined, but the semantics of the data it returns are not. STRUCTURAL_ONLY would understate the evidence, since the behavioural contract is established, not merely the layout.
semantic_findings: The function is a constant-shape two-way field selector with a zero default. Both arms are live: 0x005ab701 and 0x005ab712 pass index 0, seventeen other reported sites pass index 1.

The default arm is defensive, not dead. No observed caller passes an index other than 0 or 1, so the i>=2 -> 0 path is exercised by no recorded call site; that makes it unreachable-in-practice, not proven-unreachable.
A null stored in either slot and an out-of-range index are indistinguishable to every caller, because both yield 0 and every inspected consumer branches on exactly that.

0x00574a20 is a wrapper that rewrites the outgoing stack word to 1 and tail-jumps here, so it can only ever reach the +0x1c arm. Its own incoming argument is a receiver candidate, not a selector; the existing pkg10-editor-dispatch record for 0x00574a20 already noted this and this batch confirms it at instruction level.

The receiver is reached through at least three different member offsets of cEditor (+0x150, +0x140) and through +0xe0 of a non-editor object in 0x005ab5c0, so the two slots are not editor-specific by construction and the owning type is left opaque.

Sibling accessor 0x004c4630 returns the byte at receiver+0x84 on the same receiver class, so +0x84 is another field of the same object. It is not read by this target and is recorded only as layout context.
The whole function is 25 instructions of which 14 are frame management and stack shuffling; the observable core is two CMP/JZ pairs, one dword load per arm, and an XOR EAX,EAX default.
unresolved_questions: What concrete type owns slots +0x18 and +0x1c? Three different receiver provenances (cEditor+0x150, cEditor+0x140, unrelated+0xe0) and no located vtable mean no single owner can be named.
What do the two slots point at? 0x005ab717 shows the returned value is dereferenced at +0x34 and 0x0058c585 at +0x8, so it is an object pointer, but the object type is unresolved.
Is the i>=2 -> 0 default a shipped guard or a compiler-generated default for an enum-like selector? No caller in this batch ever passes i >= 2, so the answer is not observable statically.
Which writer maintains the two slots? No store to receiver+0x18 or receiver+0x1c was located in this batch, so the invariant that keeps them non-null at the observed call sites is unverified.
The 0x00574a20 wrapper forces index 1 regardless of its own incoming argument; whether some caller relies on reaching the +0x18 arm through that wrapper was not established.
Fifteen of the thirty-three code xrefs were not disassembled window-by-window in this batch; their receiver provenances and result uses come from the briefing's call graph.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace exists for this function, so the claim that both arms return live object pointers is static only.
A runtime differential test would have to record the two slot values at a few of the call sites to confirm which objects are returned in practice.
The original Cell stage has never been entered in any recorded run, so no stage-level reachability claim is made for this Editor-subsystem function.

body_reconstruction.claim_scope: The 25-instruction body is reconstructed in full as machine-observable semantics. No class, no field name and no slot meaning is claimed.
preserved_semantics: index 0 selects +0x18 and index 1 selects +0x1c, in that comparison order
any other index yields the dword 0 via XOR EAX,EAX, not a byte 0
exactly one dword is read; nothing in the receiver is written
no callee, no global, no allocation, no guard
a null receiver faults on the selected load
the stack word is callee-cleaned (RET 0x4), modelled with __attribute__((thiscall))
body_reconstruction.byte_exactness: not claimed. clang++ 22.1.8 -m32 -O2 emits an offset-selecting form (mov 0x4(%esp),%edx / test / je / xor / cmp $1 / jne / mov $0x1c / jmp / mov $0x18 / mov (%ecx,%eax,1),%eax / ret $4) of 35 bytes against the original's 67. The observable behaviour, the return value, the return width and the callee-cleaned epilogue match; the frame, the spills and the encoding do not.
